**C1 cash cost rose USD 1.18/t (5.8%) from USD 20.16/t in Q4 FY2026 to USD 21.33/t in Q1 FY2027.** Maintenance (+USD 0.67/t) and volume (+USD 0.27/t) were the largest drivers; lower throughput spread fixed costs over 3.4% fewer tonnes, while a sharp jump in maintenance-order spend (USD 0.27/t → USD 0.94/t) signals unplanned repair activity.

**Why:** Maintenance-order costs tripled quarter-on-quarter (USD 1.27 m → USD 4.31 m), likely reflecting breakdown repairs; diesel efficiency deteriorated (queue time and haul-distance increases visible in FMS), and lower ore processed (4.74 Mt → 4.58 Mt) diluted absorption.

**Action:** Prioritise a preventive-maintenance review of the top-three breakdown contributors in the maintenance-order backlog; targeting one unplanned-downtime hot-spot can recover 5–10% of the maintenance delta and improve fleet utilisation, lowering both volume and diesel levers.
